what: The photo panel is drawn in WebGL (three) so the grain (strength .09) always shimmers — on hover the RGB splits sideways by .006 (τ .08s), and for .3s from the moment the pointer enters, a glitch hits where 28% of 24 horizontal bands jump ±3% and split once more, while the cursor leaves six square cells behind (the faster it moves the larger, .01~.055 of panel height) in which RGB splits up to .012, the bands warp and brighten, then vanish at ~.25s. With reveal: on, the panel is uncovered in 12 steps (.75s) from bottom to top as it enters the screen. When the panel moves far away the WebGL context is released, so the number of contexts does not grow however many photos a page has

options.shift: RGB split on hover (ratio to panel width), default .006
options.trail: Cursor trail cell glitch intensity, default 1 — 0 turns it off (old name curl is also accepted)
options.reveal: If on, clears away in steps when visible
options.[data-fx-part=image]: Photo (img) to draw. If none, draws a dark scene placeholder in the clothing color and writes data-label below
options.fx:reveal: Send to the element to restart the reveal from the beginning — detail { delay, dur } Delay and duration (s) can be given with this (in the original, the first photo uses .12s when the panel is ready)
options.fx:glitch: Send to an element for one glitch (on section change or slide advance)

note: Of the original shader’s effects (grain, brightness-threshold glitch, RGB drift, mask, swirl, dithering, sand particles), only grain, hover RGB, band glitch, cursor-trail cell glitch and stair-step reveal were rewritten with the same numeric feel. The dithering transition and sand particles were not ported. Load this folder’s three-global.js before three.cjs and it can be read as window.THREE
